texts.exact_text: indicates that (under its conditions) there will be great progress and success. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. There will (then) be no error.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 17; scan-backed transcription p. 93, hexagram statement

texts.exact_text: The first NINE, undivided, shows us one changing the object of his pursuit; but if he be firm and correct, there will he good fortune. Going beyond (his own) gate to find associates, he will achieve merit.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 17; scan-backed transcription p. 93, line 1

texts.exact_text: The second SIX, divided, shows us one who cleaves to the little boy, and lets go the man of age and experience.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 17; scan-backed transcription p. 93, line 2

texts.exact_text: The third SIX, divided, shows us one who cleaves to the man of age and experience, and lets go. the little boy. Such following will get what it seeks; but it will be advantageous to adhere to what is firm and correct.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 17; scan-backed transcription p. 93, line 3

texts.exact_text: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows us one followed and obtaining (adherents). Though he be firm and correct, there will be evil. If he be sincere (however) in his course, and make that evident, into what error will he fall?
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 17; scan-backed transcription p. 93, line 4

texts.exact_text: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows us (the ruler) sincere in (fostering all) that is excellent. There will be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 17; scan-backed transcription p. 93, line 5

texts.exact_text: The topmost SIX, divided, shows us (that sincerity) firmly held and clung to, yea, and bound fast. (We see) the king with it presenting his offerings on the western mountain.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 17; scan-backed transcription p. 93, line 6

texts.exact_text:
**䷐ Suí** symbolises the idea of following. It is said to follow [**䷏ Yǜ**](e8b1abyu.md), the symbol of harmony and satisfaction.
Where there are these conditions men are sure to follow; nor will they follow those in whom they have no complacency.
The hexagram includes the cases where one follows others, and where others follow him;
and the auspice of great progress and success is due to this flexibility and applicability of it.
But in both cases the following must be guided by a reference to what is proper and correct. See the notes on the [Tuàn](https://ctext.org/book-of-changes/tuan-zhuan) and the [Great Symbolism](https://ctext.org/book-of-changes/xiang-zhuan).

Line 1 is strong, and lord of the lower trigram ☳. The weak lines ought to follow it; but here it is below them, in the lowest place of the figure. This gives rise to the representation of one changing his pursuit. Still through the native vigour indicated by the line being strong, and in its correct place, its subject will be fortunate. Going beyond his gate to find associates indicates his public spirit, and superiority to selfish considerations.

Line 2 is weak. Its proper correlate is the strong 5; but it prefers to cleave to the line below, instead of waiting to follow 5. Hence the symbolism of the text, the bad omen of which needs not to be mentioned.

Line 3 is also weak, but it follows the strong line above it and leaves line 1, reversing the course of 2; -- with a different issue. It is weak, however, and 4 is not its proper correlate; hence the conclusion of the paragraph is equivalent to a caution.

Line 4 is strong, and in the place of a great minister next the ruler in 5. But his having adherents may be injurious to the supreme and sole authority of that ruler, and only a sincere loyalty will save him from. error and misfortune.

Line 5 is strong, and in its correct place, with 2 as its proper correlate; thus producing the auspicious symbolism.

The issue of the hexagram is seen in line 6; which represents the ideal of following, directed by the most sincere adherence to what is right. This influence not only extends to men, but also to spiritual beings. `The western hill` is [mountain Qí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qishan_County), at the foot of which was the original settlement of the house of [Zhōu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_dynasty), in B. C. 1325. The use of the name `king` here brings us down from [Wén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Wen_of_Zhou) into the time of [king Wǔ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Wu_of_Zhou) at least.

# [随 ䷐](e99a8fsui_cn.md)
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 17; scan-backed transcription p. 93, notes
texts.notes: Markdown transcription retained to preserve Legge's notes and links.

texts.exact_text: 隨，元亨利貞，无咎。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 易經卦辭

texts.exact_text: 隨，剛來而下柔，動而說，隨。大亨貞，无咎，而天下隨時，隨時之義大矣哉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 彖

texts.exact_text: 澤中有雷，隨。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 大象

texts.exact_text: 初九，官有渝，貞吉，出門交有功。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 爻 1

texts.exact_text: 官有渝，從正吉也；出門交有功，不失也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 小象 1

texts.exact_text: 六二，係小子，失丈夫。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 爻 2

texts.exact_text: 係小子，弗兼與也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 小象 2

texts.exact_text: 六三，係丈夫，失小子，隨有求得，利居貞。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 爻 3

texts.exact_text: 係丈夫，志舍下也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 小象 3

texts.exact_text: 九四，隨有獲，貞凶。有孚在道以明，何咎？
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 爻 4

texts.exact_text: 隨有獲，其義凶也；有孚在道，明功也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 小象 4

texts.exact_text: 九五，孚于嘉，吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 爻 5

texts.exact_text: 孚于嘉吉，位正中也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 小象 5

texts.exact_text: 上六，拘係之，乃從維之，王用亨于西山。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 爻 6

texts.exact_text: 拘係之。上窮也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/随; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 17, 小象 6

texts.exact_text:
In ䷐ Suí we see the strong (trigram ☳) come and place itself under the weak; we see (in the two) the attributes of movement and pleasure: -- this gives (the idea of) ䷐ Suí.

'There will be great progress and success; and through firm correctness no error:' -- all under heaven will be found following at such a time.

Great indeed are the time and significance indicated in ䷐ Suí.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix I, Hexagram 17, p. unpaginated transcription

texts.exact_text: (The trigram ☵ for the waters of) a marsh and (☳ that for) thunder (hidden) in the midst of it form ䷐ Suí. The superior man in accordance with this, when it is getting towards dark, enters (his house) and rests.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 17, p. 290

texts.exact_text: 'He is changing the object of his pursuit:' -- but if he follow what is correct, there will be good fortune. 'He goes beyond (his own) gate to find associates:' -- he will not fail (in the method he pursues).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 17, line 1, p. 290

texts.exact_text: 'He cleaves to the little boy:' -- he cannot be with the two at the same time.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 17, line 2, p. 290

texts.exact_text: 'He cleaves to the man of age and experience:' -- by the decision of his will, he abandons (the youth) below.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 17, line 3, p. 290

texts.exact_text: 'He is followed and obtains adherents:' -- according to the idea (of the hexagram), this is evil. 'He is sincere in his course:' -- showing his intelligence, and leading to achievement.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 17, line 4, p. 290

texts.exact_text: 'He is sincere in fostering what is excellent:' -- his position is correct and in the centre.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 17, line 5, p. 290

texts.exact_text: 'The sincerity is firmly held and clung to, as shown in the topmost line:' -- (the idea of the hexagram) has reached its extreme development.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 17, line 6, p. 290
